meta.title: Deploying to Cloudflare
meta.description: Publish your Vanilla Press site to Cloudflare Pages with a Worker for content negotiation. Static speed, dynamic flexibility.

children.value: Vanilla Press publishes a static site to
. Cloudflare Pages serves the static files at the edge. A thin Cloudflare Worker sits in front to handle content negotiation — routing
requests to the markdown output, JSON requests to the API files, and HTML fragment requests to the fragment files.

blocks.value:
Browser/Agent
     │
     ▼
Cloudflare Worker (content negotiation)
     │
     ├── Accept: text/html      → /posts/css-layers/index.html
     ├── Accept: text/markdown   → /md/posts/css-layers/index.md
     ├── Accept: application/json → /api/posts/css-layers.json
     └── X-Star-Request: content → /posts/css-layers/_fragment.html
     │
     ▼
Cloudflare Pages (static files at edge)

children.value: The Worker adds about 1ms of latency. Every response is still served from static files — the Worker just routes to the right one. No database, no server-side rendering, no cold starts.
This authenticates with your Cloudflare account. You'll need a free Cloudflare account at minimum.
On first deploy, Wrangler creates the Pages project. Subsequent deploys update the static assets. Each deploy gets a unique preview URL.
The Worker handles content negotiation by inspecting the
header and routing to the appropriate static file variant.
In the Cloudflare dashboard, go to Pages → your project → Custom domains. Add your domain. Cloudflare handles SSL automatically — no certificate configuration needed.
The content negotiation Worker is intentionally simple. Here's the core logic:
which serves from Cloudflare Pages. This means the Worker doesn't handle caching, compression, or edge distribution — Pages does all of that.
Automate publishing on every push to

blocks.value:
name: Deploy
on:
  push:
    branches: [main]

jobs:
  deploy:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20
      - run: npm ci
      - run: node src/build/publish.js
      - uses: cloudflare/pages-action@v1
        with:
          apiToken: ${{ secrets.CF_API_TOKEN }}
          accountId: ${{ secrets.CF_ACCOUNT_ID }}
          projectName: my-site
          directory: _site
